findings.title: Invalid pasted amounts crash instead of producing an error
findings.explanation: Double(text) returns nil for invalid input such as "abc" or an empty string. Force-unwrapping that result crashes the process, violating the stated requirement that invalid amounts produce an error.
findings.recommendation: Return a throwing or Result-based API and handle failed conversion without force-unwrapping.
findings.suggested_test: After adding explicit error handling, pass "abc" and "" and assert an invalid-amount error is returned or thrown. Pass "12.50" and assert the result equals 12.5.

findings.title: Invalid amount input crashes the process
findings.explanation: Double(text) returns nil for invalid input. Force-unwrapping it traps, so arbitrary pasted text such as "abc" crashes the process instead of producing the required error. An attacker able to supply this input could trigger denial of service in the consuming process.
findings.recommendation: Use guarded optional binding and return or throw a validation error when conversion fails.
findings.suggested_test: Pass "abc" and an empty string; assert that each produces a validation error without crashing.

findings.title: Invalid input crashes instead of reporting a parsing error
findings.explanation: Force-unwrapping the failable Double initializer traps for invalid pasted text such as "abc" or an empty string. The process crashes instead of producing the required error.
findings.recommendation: Make parseAmount throwing and use guard let to unwrap Double(text), throwing a defined invalid-amount error when conversion fails.
findings.suggested_test: Pass "abc" and an empty string and assert that each produces an invalid-amount error without crashing; assert that "12.50" returns 12.5.
